methodology.timing: Process wall in measurements; library wall excluding TPC-H pool initialization in library_measurements. Library timing includes table/session/job creation, worker startup/join, generation and batch consumption.
methodology.cpu_and_rss: Whole fresh process, including setup. Ordered Populate consumers run on the calling thread; reference partitions consume/drop on their workers. Reference comparisons therefore include delivery-semantics differences; before/after comparisons keep the ordered API.
methodology.output: Full Arrow RecordBatches are generated and consumed; no IPC encoding, file output, disk flushing or cache drops.
methodology.scale: SF1, SF10 and SF100, generation only; seven measured runs after one excluded warmup.
methodology.batch_defaults: Populate TPC-H/SSB 8192, TPC-DS/DSB 2048, Rust references 8000; batch/chunk overrides remain zero.
methodology.reference: Rust tpchgen/tpchgen-arrow and tpcdsgen/tpcdsgen-arrow 4.0.0. Reference tables use up to the requested number of source partitions, including small TPC-DS tables.
methodology.aggregate: Selected tables follow TableName::ALL unless explicitly listed. The multi-thread reference adapter pops table/partition jobs from a shared Vec in LIFO order. Populate schedules remaining work per source and fuses compatible TPC-DS sales/returns. Aggregate speedups include scheduling and fusion differences; aggregate times cannot be obtained by adding isolated table times.
methodology.controls: stream consumes/drops each batch on its worker; TPC-DS stream is unfused. Do not attribute an ordered-fused versus stream-unfused difference solely to buffering.
methodology.sampling: Fresh processes, baseline/candidate order alternates each trial. No timing runs overlap builds, tests, full-output hashing or CPU profiling.
methodology.source: Main pinned at 702eebd7 when the user requested a rebase. Candidate is rebased directly onto that commit; source trees and binary SHA-256 hashes identify the measured artifacts.

learning_list.status: Measured changes are retained only after fresh-main timing and output checks. Complex opportunities below are hypotheses, not promised speedups.

retained.reason: Expose enough independent jobs for small and medium tables while limiting retained batches; preserve configured upper bounds, sequential behavior and writer chunking.

retained.change: Scope larger work units to large SSB lineorder
retained.reason: The old shared cap made SF100 regular lineorder slower. The targeted refinement reduced the pre-rebase seven-run median from 631.112 to 595.225 ms, at the cost of higher RSS; flattened rows retain the small cap.

retained.change: Retain sufficiently partitioned TPC-DS channel chunks
retained.reason: After the Distribution rewrite, applying the fixed small cap to already well-partitioned SF100 channels regressed performance. Preserve configured channel chunks when there are at least four per worker; keep adaptive dimensions and smaller channels.
Sales channels retain their configured chunks to amortize generator setup. Fresh-main measurements cover the rewritten Distribution engine and upstream checkpoint/cache improvements.

rejected.result: SF100 aggregate 3366.752 to 3442.834 ms; single-thread SF10 7996.376 to 8330.541 ms. Store channel code grew from 14032 to 14964 bytes; static stack-address memory sites rose from 326 to 367. Reverted.
rejected.interpretation: Code growth and more stack accesses are observations, not proof of the dynamic slowdown mechanism. The experiment would need repetition for the rewritten engine.

rejected.result: Helped regular SSB but raised TPC-H and flat SSB memory without improving time. Retained only the scoped SSB lineorder policy.
SF100 inventory 215.658 to 222.379 ms; no aggregate gain. Reverted. Current main has independently replaced this preparation with per-run key offsets, so this proposal is obsolete.

rejected.change: Grow every TPC-DS chunk at large scales
rejected.result: SF10 491.072 to 506.212 ms; SF100 4955.352 to 4967.820 ms, with RSS rising from 2.611 to 8.833 GiB. Reverted in favor of the channel-only exception.

complex_opportunities.change: Batch independent text-pool reads and test prefetch distances or a vectorized view-construction loop.
complex_opportunities.reason: The scalar assembly uses indexed pool loads; hiding latency depends on the actual CPU/cache behavior and sufficient independent work. Short strings and view prefixes require different handling.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Identical values and Arrow view ownership; SF1/10/100 paired samples, cache/memory counters, more than one architecture before a general policy.

complex_opportunities.change: Generate independent RNG lanes and derived columns in larger blocks, reducing intermediate per-row work.
complex_opportunities.reason: Variable child counts, exact per-source RNG budgets and skip-ahead state constrain fusion and SIMD. A faster RNG alone can move the bottleneck to row materialization.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Whole-output hashes plus adversarial chunk, batch and skip boundaries; per-table and aggregate timings and memory.

complex_opportunities.change: Batch pricing inputs, hoist invariant limits and fuse selected RNG/column passes while preserving exact integer decimal arithmetic.
complex_opportunities.reason: Large channel functions are already expensive; broader inlining was harmful in the old engine. Integer rounding, returns coupling, null selection and RNG draw budgets must remain exact.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Current-engine assembly, instruction and cycle counts, complete sales/returns hashes and paired SF1/10/100 benchmarks.

complex_opportunities.change: Bound the ordered reorder window and explore persistent workers or reusable scratch buffers.
complex_opportunities.reason: Must retain caller-thread callbacks, per-table ordering, cancellation and arbitrary downstream retention of Arrow arrays. Backpressure can introduce idle workers or deadlocks.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Slow consumer and early cancellation stress tests, duplicate/empty tables, peak RSS versus throughput, and proof buffers are never reused while retained.

complex_opportunities.change: Skip null-free bitmap blocks or attach validity while building arrays, avoiding unnecessary transpose/rebuild work.
complex_opportunities.reason: Current main already uses packed masks and a 64x64 transpose. The observed CPU share is modest, so this is lower priority than channels and pricing.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Sparse/dense/all-null masks and partial blocks; schema/nullability equality; demonstrate aggregate benefit rather than only a bitmap microbenchmark.

complex_opportunities.change: Prebind exponential-rank lookup tables and investigate sharing immutable keyed permutations across compatible generator instances.
complex_opportunities.reason: Main already shares rank tables, densifies checkpoints and builds attribute maps in parallel. Permutation reuse must key every seed/range dependency and advance RNG state by the exact number of consumed draws; table prebinding must preserve exact step boundaries and fallback cases.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Separate cold-process startup from repeated in-process generation, verify random chunk/skip order and full values, and measure cache memory as well as CPU time.
complex_opportunities.evidence: Fresh SF10 DSB profile: exp_rank 18.92% and make_key_perm 14.32% of sampled user cycles. Rows<G> opens a generator at each chunk start; customer and item constructors build permutations.

Retained for the primary SF10 target (7.8% faster) and SF100 memory reduction (5.46 to 4.23 GiB) with neutral SF100 time.
